Q01 Facebook Ads

What is custom audience and lookalike audience, how are they different? How do we set them up on the platform. Difference between 1% lookalike and 9% lookalike?

To create a custom audience on Facebook, we can submit a list of users. This list includes the names, phone numbers, email addresses, and other details of our current clients.

When we use this list of users from our custom audience and tell Facebook to show our ads to users who are similar to those on our provided list,these audience are known as "lookalike targeting."

Custom Audiences can be created on the platform by uploading CRM lists, using lists of people who have visited our website in the past or taken an action, or might have interacted with our ad creatives.

Lookalike audience can be created by making a custom lookalike list along with the desired percentage of people that we want the platform to find for us based on our custom list and making sure that the type of audience is very similar to our custom list based audience.

The audience size grows the further we deviate from 1%, but the drawback is that the audience becomes less relatable in comparison to our custom list-based audience. For instance: In comparison to a 9% Lookalike, a 1% Lookalike audience would look much relevant to the audience list that we have uploaded. In 1% Lookalike, the audience base would be smaller but more relevant to our custom list whereas in 9% Lookalike, the audience base would be much larger but the relevancy would decline.

Q02 Facebook Ads

What are the different ad placements available for Facebook?

In Facebook ad placements are of 4 types :-

1. Facebook - Places in Facebook include Facebook News Feed, Facebook Marketplace, Facebook right column, Facebook Stories, Facebook in-stream videos, Facebook search results, Facebook Instant Articles,

2. Instagram - Places in Instagram include Instagram feed, Instagram Explore, Instagram Shop, Instagram Stories, Instagram in-stream videos, Instagram Reels

3. Messenger - Places in Messenger include Messenger Inbox, Messenger Stories, Messenger sponsored messages

4. Audience Network - Places in Audience Network include Audience Network native, banner and interstitial, Audience Network rewarded videos. Facebook Audience Network is an off-Facebook, in-app advertising network for mobile apps. Advertisers can serve up their ads to customers who are using mobile sites and apps other than Facebook, extending their reach beyond the platform while still getting to use Facebook's exceptionally powerful ad system.

Q03 Google Ads

Explain the different bidding strategies in both Facebook & Google

Facebook :

1. Lowest Cost - Facebook will try to win ad spots for us at the lowest cost available. The goal is to get as many ad spots as possible for our budget. The platform will aim to spend all the way up to our budget limit as fast as possible.

2. Cost Cap - Cost cap bidding works by setting a limit on the average cost per action (CPA). Facebook will bid higher for some ad spots and lower for others, but the overall average cost will stay at or below our cost cap.

3. Bid Cap - When we choose bid cap, it means that we set a limit on how much Facebook can bid for an ad spot. This is an advanced option. Unlike cost cap (where Facebook keeps the average bid below our limit), it acts as a hard limit on every single bid. Instead of setting a general goal, we are in charge of each individual ad spot. If we want to use it, we’ll need to have an accurate estimate of what our ad spots might cost so we don’t accidentally set our bid cap too low and miss out on spots. We’ll also have to keep an eye on the campaign so that we can update the bid cap as necessary.

Google :

1. Target cost per action (tCPA): If we want to optimize for conversions, we can use Target CPA to help increase conversions while targeting a specific cost per action (CPA).

2. Target return on ad spend (tROAS): If we want to optimize for conversion value, we can use Target ROAS to help increase conversion value while targeting a specific return on ad spend (ROAS).

3. Maximize Conversions: If we want to optimize for conversions, but just want to spend our entire budget instead of targeting a specific CPA, we can use Maximize Conversions.

4. Maximize Conversion Value: If we want to optimize for conversion value, but just want to spend our entire budget instead of targeting a specific ROAS, we can use Maximize Conversion Value.

5. Enhanced cost per click (ECPC): If we want to automatically adjust our manual bids to try to maximize conversions, we can use ECPC. It’s an optional feature we can use with Manual CPC bidding.

6. Maximize Clicks: This is an automated bid strategy. It's the simplest way to bid for clicks. All we have to do is set an average daily budget, and the Google Ads system automatically manages our bids to bring us the most clicks possible within our budget.

7. Manual CPC bidding: This let us manage our maximum CPC bids ourself. we can set different bids for each ad group in our campaign, or for individual keywords or placements. If we've found that certain keywords or placements are more profitable, we can use manual bidding to allocate more of our advertising budget to those keywords or placements.

8. Target Impression Share: Automatically sets bids with the goal of showing our ad on the absolute top of the page, on the top of the page, or anywhere on the page of Google search results.

9. CPM: With this bid strategy, we’ll pay based on the number of impressions (times our ads are shown) that we receive on the Google Display Network.

10. tCPM: A bidding strategy where we set an average for how much we’re willing to pay for every thousand impressions. It optimizes bids to maximize our campaign’s unique reach. With tCPM, we can keep our campaign’s average CPM lower or equal to the target we set (although the cost of impressions may vary).

11. vCPM: This is a manual bidding strategy we can use if our ads are designed to increase awareness, but not necessarily generate clicks or traffic. It lets us set the highest amount we want to pay for each 1,000 viewable ad impressions on the Google Display Network.

12. CPV: With this bid strategy, we’ll pay based on the number of views (times our video ads are shown) that we receive on the YouTube.

Q05 Google Ads

What is the use of Google search console and Google analytics?

The free Google Search Console service enables users to track website traffic, examine keyword performance, address problems, and receive notifications from Google about their website. It offers information on how a website is performing in organic search as well as suggestions for improving the site's indexing by Google. (Contrary to Google Analytics, Search Console only offers data on traffic that originates from web searches; it excludes additional segments including direct traffic, traffic from adverts, and traffic from site referrals.)

Google Analytics is used to track website performance and collect visitor insights. Organizations can use it to identify the main user traffic sources, evaluate the effectiveness of their marketing initiatives and campaigns, track goal accomplishments (like purchases and cart additions), identify patterns and trends in user engagement, and gather other visitor data like demographics. Google Metrics is frequently used by small and medium-sized retail websites to gather and analyse different customer behaviour analytics, which can be utilised to enhance marketing campaigns, increase website traffic, and better retain customers.

Q06 Google Ads

Explain the setup of a Google search campaign with a step by step process

Step 1: Go to the Google Ads Website

Go to https://ads.google.com. You will then see, “Start Now.” Click on that and sign up for your Google Ads account. You can then click on the button that says, “Create your first campaign.”

Step 2: Choose a Campaign Type and Name

You have options for a campaign type. When you’re just getting started, it’s best to choose “Search Network only.”

Name your campaign. You may want to choose a name that has to do with the product or service you’re advertising.

Step 3: Select Ad Display Location

You have many options when it comes to people’s locations. You can choose a large or small area. For instance, an entire country or just a city. If you want a specific area, you can use latitude-longitude coordinates.

Be sure you know the locations of your ideal customer. If you’re a local business owner, you want to target people around your area. If you’re selling your products and services to people throughout the United States, choose the U.S. For business owners who sell internationally, you may want to set up several campaigns for countries that have the highest sales or where most of your consumers live.

Step 4: Set Your Daily Budget

Until you become a proficient Google Ads user, it’s best to set a low daily budget. This allows you to start slowly, gather data, and then expand what’s working once you are more familiar with your campaigns. Note that Google can and will go slightly over your daily budget. For that reason, it’s important to keep a close eye on your campaigns and adjust your budgets each week to ensure you don’t go over your maximum monthly ad budget.

Step 5: Add Keywords

This can be tricky, especially for first time advertisers. Your first inclination is likely to add as many keywords as possible that you think are relevant for your business. In fact, this is exactly what Google wants you to do because then you’ll spend more money.

These are the keywords where there is absolutely no doubt that the person searching the keyword is looking for exactly what you offer. There may only be a handful of these bullseye keywords and that’s OK. Don’t add any keywords where there is any doubt the searcher may not be looking for your product or service.

Step 6: Create an Ad

This is when the fun begins. You get to create an ad that will attract your consumers and make them click to go to your website. Prospects are more likely to click on an ad that has the keyword they used in Google’s search bar. So, if you are targeting a specific keyword phrase your consumers use (after doing keyword research), be sure to use that phrase in one of the two headlines.

After the headlines, you can move on to the ad description. Focus on the key benefits of your product or service, describe your special offer if you have one, and end with a strong call to action.

Lastly, it is recommend sending people to a landing page that is created to specifically match your ad. By doing this, you can ensure that the information in the ad is reflected on the landing page, which will lead to stronger conversions. People often make the mistake of setting up an ad that advertises a special deal and then sending them to their homepage that never mentions this deal. This only leads to frustration on the part of your prospect. A landing page should be highly targeted for the keyword phrase you used in your ad.

Step 7: Set Up Conversion Tracking

This last step is to set up all the appropriate conversion tracking for your business. Google gives you the following options:

Webform leads (ex. quote requests)

E-commerce orders (ex. orders from your online shopping cart)

Calls from ads (ex. phone calls from the number displayed on your ads)

Calls from the website (ex. phone calls from the number displayed on your website)

Imports from sales that occur off of the internet

Q08 Fundamentals

What's the difference b/w traditional and digital marketing

Traditional Marketing: The traditional marketing technique is an outdated method of advertising. Flyers, billboards, TV and radio commercials, print and newspaper ads, and other forms of advertising were used by businesses to market their goods in the early years.

Interest, awareness, desire, and decision-making are the four stages of traditional marketing.

Digital Marketing: A contemporary method of marketing is called "digital marketing." Through web marketing, we promote and sell goods and services. Additionally, it describes the marketing of any kind of business using online platforms and tools like Google, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, etc.

Digital marketing involves four stages: planning, conversation, content, and sequences.

Q09 Fundamentals

Major difference between FB and Google ads

Google Ads is a type of marketplace or online advertising platform created by Google where we can advertise our company online with the aid of keywords or display ads, product listings, and service offerings within the Google Ads network. Keyword research is the main focus of Google advertising. If we use the best keyword for them, our advertising will show up on Google's first page, making it simpler for visitors to find them.

Facebook Ads are a form of internet advertising that emphasises social networking services that enable advertisements to reach a targeted audience and analyse that audience's interests, purchasing trends, activity, and usage. Age, gender, and geographic information about the target audience are also provided. Around 1.18 million people use Facebook every day.

Facebook ads are based on CPM model whereas Google ads are based on CPM model. Facebook Ads and Google Ads have quite different use cases. For businesses, items, or services like plumbers that our audience is actively looking for, Google Ads works best. Facebook Ads, also known as Meta Ads or Meta for Business, work best for promoting products that our target market is likely to be interested in but isn't necessarily actively searching for, like new headphones

Q10 Fundamentals

Diffrence between affinity and in- marketing

Affinity Audiences:

We can reach out to potential clients using this kind of targeted technique to spread the word about our business. The audience can relate to these advertising because of the situation. Affinity Audiences are people who have a broad, enduring interest that is aligned with a particular Affinity Segment. This targeting choice looks at audience development more long-term. Affinity targeting examines someone's complete interests, passions, and lifestyle rather than just one specific purchase intent, like In-market, to gain a deeper idea of who they are as a whole.

In-Market Audiences:

In-Market audiences reach out to potential customers who are actively researching or looking to buy products and services. It helps us to target potential customers who are more likely to make a conversion.

For instance, if our company sells laptops as an electronics brand, we can target customers who are actively shopping for or researching laptops using in-market audiences.

Q11 Facebook Ads

What is R & F

R&F stands for Reach and Frequency. An R&F Campaign is a special type of Facebook media buy that allows brands to plan and predict the reach and frequency of posts by confirming the reach of certain percentages of target audiences based on timing, desired frequency, target, and budget.

R&F buying guidelines are as follows:

1. Ad sets must be 1-90 days in length and can be booked six months in advance of our launch date.

2. We have to must reach a minimum of 200,000 people per Ad Set.

3. We are setting a frequency cap, not a target. FB will not go over our frequency cap.

4. Campaigns cannot be paused but only can be cancelled.

5. Ads must be uploaded to the adsets within six hours after the sceduled start time. If they are uploaded after that, the Ad Set will be cancelled.

6. Each Ad Set has its own Budget, Reach, Frequency, Targeting and Placements.

7. We cannot exclude dynamic audiences such as: Website Custom Audiences, Video Viewer Audiences, Fans, Friends of Connections.

Q12 Strategy & Planning

Difference between seo and sem and how it benefits the business

In contrast to Search Engine Optimisation(SEO), which focuses solely on getting traffic from organic search, Search Engine Marketing (SEM) focuses on acquiring traffic from both organic and paid search.

The process of improving a website's rankings on specific search engines using unpaid online advertising is known as SEO. It is used to increase traffic to a website by improving its ranking on search engine results pages.

SEM is the process of using paid advertisements to increase a website's visibility in search engine results pages. It consists of various strategies such as SEO, contextual marketing, AdSense, social networking, pay-per-click (PPC), and AdWords.

We have a better chance of bringing in high-quality visitors and increasing conversion rates when SEO and SEM are properly configured. The foundation of successful SEM is SEO. If our website is SEO-friendly and our sponsored ads are properly targeted using the right keywords, we have a better chance of ranking at the top of paid searches. However, our SEO must be in place for Google to consider our website to be credible. If our website is relatively new, we can prioritise our PPC campaign initially because SEO rankings can take some time to establish themselves. This is how they both work together and benefit the business.

Q13 Strategy & Planning

If we are launching a new soft drink how will we strategize it?

For Facebook, I would do it in three stages:- Awareness, Consideration and Conversion.

Awareness (Pre Launch):

Prior to the release of the Soft Drink, we will run an awareness campaign to generate buzz.

We won't unveil the Soft drink; we'll tease the launch and let people know when it will happen.

This pre-launch campaign will begin two weeks before the launch, and the campaign will conclude one day before the launch.

To ensure that a greater number of people see the advertisement and learn about the launch, we will use a 15-second video and optimise the campaign for thruplays.

Awareness:

The awareness campaign will consist of three adsets

People interested in Soft Drinks will be the target audience in adset 1.

Then, we will focus on young people between the ages of 18 and 26 in Adset 2. College-bound students make up the majority of this demographic, and they are particularly interested in Soft Drinks.

The third ad set will consist of those people who follow our competitors.

To ensure that a greater number of people see the advertisement and learn about the newly launched product, we will use a 15-second video and optimise the campaign for thruplays.

Consideration Phase:

The consideration campaign will drive traffic to the website.

The target audience for the website campaign will be previous website visitors that we will be retargeting. Then, another ad set will target people who went to a specific product page. Additionally, we'll retarget individuals who viewed our awareness campaign ad for at least 15 seconds.

we will also select one core audience from the awareness campaigns because it performed fairly well.

Conversion Phase:

The conversion campaign will conversion from the website,

The website conversion campaign will consist of the following audience:-

Website visitors with a frequency greater than 4 wherein people who visited a specific page for more than 4 times will be retargeted.

Lookalike of Past purchasers from website and cart abandoners.

The budget split will be 50:30:20, wherein 50percent of the budget will be alloted to the awareness phase, 30percent to the consideration phase and 20percent to the conversion phase.

Q14 Strategy & Planning

Suppose, a company is manufacturer of TV and a new one, we have to make the campaign for both fb and google, share me our thought process for the same? Objective is sale

Since the tv brand is new, we would employ a marketing funnel to push consumers down the funnel. We could use both the Facebook and Google advertising networks, but we would give Google advertising higher attention for the sale parts. On Facebook, we would conduct an awareness phase with our targeted consumer group, age 25 to 50, male and female, throughout all of India, showcasing interests in electronics and the brands of our competitors.

By utilising engaging video ad creative that highlights our USP and fantastic offers on our goods. We can execute traffic and video views campaigns during the deliberation stage to boost the likelihood that users will consider purchasing our product. To maximise sales during the sales phase, we can run website conversion, catalogue sale, and store traffic campaigns.

The majority of the time, we would conduct a search sales campaign for google advertising, focusing on branded, generic, and rival TV-related keywords. Additionally, we would execute shopping campaigns while allocating the majority of the expenditures to these two categories. To get the most awareness out of our budget during the awareness phase, we would use the target impression share strategy on a variety of Google platforms, including search, display, and youtube. For youtube and display, we could use contextual targeting, such as channels and websites related to technology and electronics. We would also create custom intent and custom affinity segments to be more precise with targeting. We may execute website traffic on search advertisements and product and brand consideration campaigns for YouTube during the product consideration phase. We can then launch RLSA ads for specifically targeting folks for our sales goal after we have adequate traffic on our website. We may allocate more funds to sales and shopping campaigns on Google because the in-market sector of the search engine is the best and those audiences have the highest conversion intent.

Q15 YouTube & Video

Different type of weTube ads, which is suitable for which type of campaign and why?

Available video ad formats include:

Skippable in-stream ads - Campaign types include Sales, Leads, Traffic, Brand Awareness and Reach, Product and brand consideration

Use skippable in-stream ads when we have video content we'd like to promote before, during, or after other videos on YouTube and across websites and apps running on Google video partners.

Non-skippable in-stream ads - Campaign types include Brand awareness and reach

Use non-skippable in-stream ads when we have video content we'd like to promote before, during, or after other videos on YouTube and across websites and apps running on Google video partners and we want viewers to view the entire message without skipping our video.

In-feed video ads - Campaign types include Product and brand consideration

Use in-feed video ads to promote video content in places of discovery, including next to related YouTube videos, as part of a YouTube search result, or on the YouTube mobile homepage.

Bumper ads - Campaign types include Brand awareness and reach

Use bumper ads when we want to reach viewers broadly with a short, memorable message.

Outstream ads

Use outstream ads when we want to expand the reach of our video ads on mobile, helping we reach more customers.

Masthead ads

Use this format when we want to drive awareness for a new product or service or reach a massive audience in a short period of time (for example, a sales event).

Q17 Google Ads

Explain Quality score? If in a situation, QS is 5 and my landing page take too time to load what should I do?

Our ad quality will be compared to that of other advertisers using a diagnostic tool called Quality Score. This rating, which ranges from 1 to 10, is available at the keyword level. A higher Quality Score indicates that, in comparison to other marketers, our ad and landing page are more pertinent and helpful to someone searching for our term.The Quality Score diagnostic tool will help us to find areas where our advertisements, landing pages, or keyword choice could be improved.

The factors that determine QS :-

1. Expected clickthrough rate (CTR): The probability that a user will click our advertisement once it appears.

2. Ad relevance: How well our advertisement corresponds to the searcher's intention.

3. Experience on the landing page: How pertinent and helpful our page is to those who click on our advertisement.

In such situation we should try to improve the quality of landing page by making it mobile friendly and faster to load. The improvement in Landing page experience will increase the QS. We should also take care of the Ad relevance by making the ad copies relevant to the landing page.

Q19 Strategy & Planning

Structure a campaign for a new startup who is selling medical equipments

for a new startup lets say for selling mediacl quipments the intial steps before creating campaigns are

1. Identify Buyer Personas

For any marketing campaign to be successful, it’s incredibly crucial to identify your target prospects, their needs, and the type of message that would appeal to them. Hence, to create an effective medical equipment marketing plan, you’ll have to start by specifying your buyer personas. Identifying the buyer personas of your target prospects allows you to understand your existing and prospective clients better—their habits, likes, preferred shopping habits, pain points, demographic info, and more. This ultimately makes it easier for you to curate content that will appeal to your prospects.

2. Analyze Your Competitors

Another great way to build a comprehensive marketing plan is by learning from your competitors. Take time to analyze their marketing activities. Your central goal is to find out which tools and medical equipment marketing method they use to attract their prospects and market their products. You should also examine how your competitors boost their website traffic and conversion rates. By determining which marketing strategies work for them and what doesn’t, you can create a solid marketing plan by improving upon your competition’s approach.

3. Develop Your Value Proposition

The next important step is to understand how your target audience can solve their real-life problems with your medical devices and develop a unique value proposition. You should determine all the benefits of the medical devices you offer and tell your prospects why these benefits can be helpful for them. Explain how your products differ and are better than your competitors’ products.

A great way would be to develop unique value propositions for different buyer personas. While your product may be the same, you just have to customize your messages based on which prospect you’re talking to.

4. Use Your Sales Team Insights

Glean all the knowledge your sales executives have obtained over the years of interaction with your target market and determine the best way to integrate that insight into your medical equipment marketing plan. The online sales process is different in various ways as compared to what your sales representatives engage in. The core remains the same—the target audience has the same issues to solve; the sales cycle stages and the triggers remain the same. These days, most sales cycles take place before the prospective customer even engages with your organization and thus, you need to recreate the steps based on the paths your leads follow to become clients.

5. Clearly Articulate the Sales Process Steps

To replicate your sales process online, you’ll need more than just a basic comprehension of the methods your sales department employ and the challenges they face. Take time to clearly articulate each phase in the process. Then, attach the concerns, questions, goals, and challenges linked with that step.

After mapping out the cycle and every related consideration, you’ll have to direct your focus on creating content that will help direct those leads down the direction toward conversions before even speaking with them. Essentially, you should determine the type of content that will lead those prospects toward each conversion point.

6. Create Your Content Strategy

To create effective content, understanding your prospects’ concerns and questions is vital, but, it’s just one part of the solution. Another key consideration is the content type and the placement that is going to be effective at specific stages. For instance, blog posts are quite effective in drawing new leads to your site, acquainting them with what you do, and showcasing your expertise. Similarly, Quora answers, Youtube videos, and other social platform posts are a great way to introduce yourself to prospective clients.

That said, prospects who are at the final stage of the buyer’s journey will expect to receive comprehensive details, followed by solid data to support your product’s value. For such cases, white papers and other high-quality content that requires one to fill a form to download will be effective.

7. Sales & Marketing Alignment

Recreating the pre-stages of the sales cycle online enables you to reach potential clients who are not yet ready to engage with your company, allows you to attract more leads, and makes it more cost-effective and easier to drive those prospects down the sales pipeline.

on the basis of evaluation of these basis we can move ahead with creating a marketing campaign.

The purchase of a medical device requires a great deal of consideration and research, and that process doesn’t happen overnight.

Because the buyer’s journey is extended for medical devices, it’s important to have information and marketing materials ready to meet the audience at each step of the decision process. The steps of the buyer’s journey typically consist of:

Awareness: Your audience becomes aware of your device’s existence through internet searches or ads. This phase of the journey includes tactics like press releases, radio and TV, online ads, and search engine optimization.

Consideration: The audience understands the problem they are facing, and knows that you have a device that may help. In the consideration phase, customers look for information that will aid them in understanding the product’s effectiveness and clinical results. Content like social ads, email marketing, marketing automation, and blogs are part of the consideration phase.

Purchase: In the purchase or decision stage, the buyer has done their research and is ready to make a decision on the product that will best meet their needs. Product comparisons, ROI analysis, and device guides help the audience make the decision to buy. Testimonials and case studies are powerful assets that back your product’s claims with real-world results. Online sample or demo requests, contact centers, and e-commerce functionality promote self-service purchases.

Ensuring that you can answer a buyer’s questions at each step of the journey will paint a complete picture of the value of your device. The intent is to answer questions before the buyer asks while walking through the competitive advantages of your product versus other options. When done effectively, this full journey approach to your marketing asset plan will lead your audience from one decision stepping stone to the next, impressing upon the customer the value and meaning of the outcomes for both doctors and patients.

Q22 Google Ads

Explain the different automatic bidding strategies in google ads

The automated bidding strategies in Google Ads include :-

Maximize Clicks - To assist we achieve as many clicks as we can within our budget, maximise clicks automatically sets our bids. It is possible to maximise clicks using either a portfolio bid strategy over numerous campaigns or a regular strategy in a single campaign.

Target impression share - Target Impression Share automatically sets bids to display our ad anywhere on the page of Google search results, including at the very top of the page.

Target CPA - To assist we achieve the target cost-per-action (CPA) that we define, Target CPA automatically sets bids. Some conversions could cost more or less than what we were hoping for.

Target ROAS - In order to maximise conversion value at the goal return on ad spend (ROAS) we choose, Target ROAS automatically adjusts bids. Some conversions could return more or less than what we expected.

Maximize conversions - Maximize conversions bidding will help we optimize towards conversions.

Maximize conversion value - In order to assist we acquire the maximum conversion value for our campaign while sticking to our budget, maximise conversion value automatically sets bids.

Q23 Google Ads

What is auction insight & how can we use it?

Auction Insight help us to analyse the campaign performance with competitors based on the Campaigns, adgroup, Keywords.

Impression share -

Position Above rate - Position above rate is how often the other advertiser’s ad was shown in a higher position than my was, when both of ours ads were shown at the same time. For example, if one of the other advertisers in our auction insights report is showing “5%” in the “Position above rate” column, this means that the other advertiser’s ad showed in a position above my ads in 5 out of every 100 times our ads showed at the same time.

Overlap rate - Overlap rate is how often another advertiser’s ad received an impression when my ad also received an impression. For example, if one of the other advertisers in our auction insights report is showing “60%” in the “Overlap rate” column, this means that in 6 out of every 10 times our ad showed, an ad from this advertiser showed as well.

Impression Share - The number of impressions we received divided by the estimated number of impressions we were eligible to receiv

Outranking share - Outranking share tells me how often my ad ranked higher in the auction than another advertiser’s ad, or if my ad showed when theirs didn’t. For example, if one of the other advertisers in our auction insights report is showing "20%" in the “Outranking share” column, this means that our ad won over the other advertiser's ad. It can also mean that our ad showed when the other advertiser's ad didn’t for 2 out of every 10 impressions that we were eligible to receive.

Top of the page rate - Top of page rate tells me how often my ad (or the ad of another advertiser, depending on which row we're viewing) was shown at the top of the page, above the unpaid search results. For example, if i had 100 impressions out of which 20 impressions appear in any of the positions above the organic search results, the top of page rate will be 20%.

Absolute top Of the page rate - Absolute top of the page rate tells me how often ad (or the ad of another advertiser, depending on which row we're viewing) was shown at the absolute top of the page as the very first ad above the organic search results. For example, if out of 100 impressions, an ad has 10 impressions in which it appears as the first ad above the organic search results, the absolute top of page rate will be 10%.

tROAS optimises for conversion value as opposed to tCPA which optimises for conversions. This means that tROAS will go after users who are likely to not just convert, but convert with more value. Q25 Facebook Ads

Difference between Lowest cost and cost cap bidding strategy, and which one to use when

Lowest Cost - This strategy allows bidding to be fully managed by Facebook. It’s widely used by beginners because there isn’t much need to fully understand the intricacies of the bidding systems and options. This bidding strategy will use our entire budget and will focus on achieving the lowest cost opportunities. Unless we have super specific budget goals in mind, this is our best bet for a Facebook bidding strategy!

When to use: When we are new marketer with no past experience | No past understsanding about brands performance | Maximise actions/conversions with available budgets

Cost Cap - This is another Facebook managed bidding strategy. It allows we to keep our overall costs within a specified limit. Rather than having to manually adjust our bids (as with the bid cap strategy), Facebook will automatically do this for we to maximize the volume within our target cost per action/conversion

When to use: When a brand does not want to spend more than a certain amount on conversions/acquisitions | When leads/conversions at a particular range have been of good quality | When campaigns are longer in duration (eg: 3 months)

Q30 Facebook Ads

If we are given an audience of 30 million and in the first week our frequency is increasing. How would we optimize our campaign if our frequency is increasing?

Set Up Frequency Rules

Setting up frequency restrictions when creating your campaigns is the simplest way to make sure your frequency doesn't rise too high.

Frequency capping

. The process you can use to limit how frequently a specific audience member sees your advertisement is called frequency capping. You can adjust your frequency based on the platform you're using to:

1. Limit the amount of times a certain advertisement or even a certain collection of advertisements is shown to a customer.

2. Adjust the frequency in accordance with various time constraints and the lead's classification in your system.

3. Depending on the nature of your campaign, test and adjust over time.

In the end, restricting the number of times an advertisement can be seen by a consumer will lessen their likelihood of developing ad fatigue and a poor opinion of your company. Setting a cap also enables you to manage your ad spending to extend the duration of the campaign, increase reach, or even spend less overall without sacrificing effectiveness.

Being able to manage as many variables as you can improves the experience for both the target audience of your campaign and the business advertising its goods and services. In addition to damage management, frequency capping also nurtures brands.

Q32 Facebook Ads

How do we reduce ad fatigue?

Steps to reduce ad fatigue :-

1. Monitor our ad campaign

The first step to preventing ad fatigue is to monitor our ad campaign. We won’t know our audience lost interest in our ads if we’re not tracking our ads’ performances. The first step to combating ad fatigue is monitoring our ad campaign to see how our audience interacts with our content.

2. monitor Frequency and CTR:

Frequency: One of the most important metrics to track for digital advertising fatigue is frequency. Frequency is the average number of times people see our ad. If our audience starts seeing our ad close to ten times, they see it too frequently.

CTR: our CTR is another metric we’ll want to monitor for ad fatigue.

our CTR is the number of times people click on our ad divided by the number of impressions. Check our industry CTR to see if we need to cycle our ad out to drive a higher CTR

By monitoring our ad campaign, we can pinpoint ad fatigue faster and alter our campaign to drive better results.

3. Create multiple ads and rotate them

Creating different versions of our ad allows we to deliver the same content in a new way. It keeps our ad content fresh for our audience because each advertisement will appear different.

Once we have different versions of our ad created, we can rotate our ads. Ad rotation is one of the top recommendations for keeping our ad content fresh and exciting. With ad rotation, we pull out ads that are underperforming and replace them with another copy of our ad.

we can choose to optimize our ad rotation, where the platform will select the ad it thinks will perform the best, given the keywords, targeting, etc.

4. refresh our ad creatives

Change the colors on our ad

Reword our ad content

Change up the visuals on our ad

Try using a different call to action (CTA)

5. change ad format, try different ad formats

current ad format may not deliver information in the best way possible for our audience. Combat ad fatigue by changing our ad format.

The kind of ad we use will depend on the platform. For example, if we’re running an ad on social media, we can try formats like:

Image ads

Video ads

Carousel ads

By changing up the ad format, we’ll present the same information in a new way that may be more interesting to our audience.

Q34 Google Ads

What is attribution? Attribution model on FB/Google.

Attribution models determine how credit is given to touchpoints for a conversion. The touchpoints that we want the attribution model to take into account are specified in attribution windows. How long before a conversion the attribution model should search for touchpoints to give credit depends on the attribution window we choose.

Facebook attribution model

Facebook Attribution by default uses a last-touch model with a 1-day impression and 28-day click window. For example, if we choose purchase as our conversion and use the default attribution model and attribution window, our reporting will include purchases that Facebook can attribute to the most recent ad click that occurred within 28 days prior to purchase or the most recent ad impression that occurred within one day of purchase, whichever occurred last.

Google attribution model

Last click: Assigns sole credit for the conversion to the most recent advertisement and associated keyword.

First click: The ad and associated keyword that received the first click receive full credit for the conversion.

Linear: All ad interactions along the path share equally in the credit for the conversion.

Time decay: Favors ad interactions that took place more recently than the conversion. The distribution of credit uses a 7-day half-life. In other words, an interaction with an advertisement eight days prior to a conversion is worth half as much as one that occurs one day prior to a conversion.

Position-based: Distributes the remaining 20% among the other ads interaction on the path, giving 40% of the credit to the first and last ad interactions and associated keywords.

Data-driven: Assigns credit for the conversion in accordance with your previous conversion action data. It differs from the other models in that it determines the actual contribution of each interaction along the conversion path using data from your account. For the majority of conversion actions, the "Data-driven" model is the default attribution model.

What is ad scheduling and where can we setup it?

You can specify specific times or days of the week when you want your ads to appear using the Google Ads scheduling tool. Set up bid adjustments to raise or lower your bids during certain days and hours.

Your Google Ads campaigns are initially configured to display ads "All day." This indicates that every day of the year, your advertisements are eligible to run. Keep in mind that if no one searches for your keywords at the specified time or day you scheduled, your ads are not going to show.

Facebook Ads Scheduling:

Step 1: Click "create" on your dashboard in Ads Manager to begin a new ad or ad set.

Step 2: Create your ad's opening components as usual. If you've never created an ad in Facebook Ads Manager before, you can learn more about setting your objective, placements, and target audience by reading our comprehensive Facebook Ads Guide. You can then move on to budget after finishing that. You must specify a total spending amount for the duration of the ad's life and set the budget to "lifetime" in order to use Facebook ad scheduling.

Step 3: Click "Edit" next to "Ad Scheduling" after choosing "Show More Options" beneath the budget details.

Step 4: Choose "Run ads on a schedule" in step four. You can select exactly when you want your advertisement to run by selecting the dates and times that will appear in a box. Facebook displays time blocks that are one-hour long. You can choose to run your advertisement daily or every day during the same time slot. You might run your advertisement only during that time slot every day of the week if, for instance, your audience is online from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

Step 5: After your advertisement has been scheduled, click "Continue" to carry out the remaining steps in ad creation. When the advertisement is published, it will begin to run on the specified schedule.

Q36 Facebook Ads

How can we setup R&F campaign?

Steps to set up a reach and frequency campaign:

1) Go to Ads Manager.

2) Choose Reach and frequency as your buying type at the Campaign level.

3) Select your objective.

4) Set your lifetime budget: The maximum sum you will spend on advertising during the course of your campaign is the lifetime budget. Your predicted results, which are displayed in Ads Manager along the right side, will adjust when your budget does to reflect your updated budget. As you alter your campaign, ad set, or advertisement that has an impact on cost, predicted results will also alter.

Enter the maximum amount you wish to spend during the course of your campaign in the Budget field at the Ad Set level.

5) Choose your Facebook Page: Under Facebook Page, make sure the Facebook Page for the company you want to run ads for is selected. If your ad account is linked to more than one Page, choose the company you want to run ads for from the drop-down menu.

6) Select the Instagram account: Choose the Instagram account, you want to link to your marketing campaign under Instagram Account. This will aid Facebook in accurately predicting the audience size of your campaign.

7) Set your ad schedule: Decide when you want your ads to appear. You can choose the time frame for which your ads will run. You can also decide when you want people to see your advertisements. After you reserve (book and purchase) your reach and frequency campaign, you can sequence your ads as you please. Find out more about ad sequencing or scheduling.

8) Define your audience: A default audience has been selected as your target audience. By choosing Edit audience in the Audience section of the Ad set level, you can change your target audience. You can use detailed or connection targeting options while editing your audience, as well as add or edit Custom Audiences.

9) Choose your placements: Decide where you want your ads to appear. If you choose automatic placements, Facebook will run your ads where they are likely to produce the best results for the least amount of money. Select Edit placements and check the box next to any placement where you don't want your ads to appear if you want to change your placements. The block list and inventory filter brand safety tools are also available.

10) Choose your delivery and optimization options: Set your Reach and frequency balance and the outcome you want to optimise your ad delivery toward. How frequently people in your target audience will see the ads in your ad set during the life of your campaign depends on your reach and frequency balance.

11) Click Continue to continue designing and producing the advertisements for your campaign.

12) When you're done with your ad creative, click Review.

13) To reserve (buy and book) your reach and frequency campaign, click Confirm.

Q40 Fundamentals

What could be the reason for the CTR fluctuations and what role do creatives play

CTR changes come from one of these key areas:-

1. Total data consistency

2. Ad changes

3. Campaign settings

4. Impression changes

5. Targeting changes

6. Budget

7. Match type usage

How Ads affect CTR

Ad Types - The ad types you use can affect CTR. RSAs usually have higher CTRs than ETAs (and lower conversion rates). As you know the message in ETAs, their data is more stable than RSAs month over month. It’s not uncommon to see an ad group or campaign that only uses RSAs to have some wide swings in CTR and conversion rates.

Ad Testing - As you introduce new ads, your CTRs will naturally change as the new ads will now be served in place of the old ads for some impressions.

Ad Rotation - When you use ‘rotate’ as your ad serving option, your CTRs are generally stable and changes in CTRs come from changes to the ads (or targeting and other areas we’ll get to) and not due to the other ads in the ad groups taking impressions from your top ads.

When you use ‘optimize’ it’s common to see some wide swings in data on occasion as Google is often optimizing for CTR (over conversion rates) and the system can make mistakes in the ad serving. These mistakes can affect your CTRs.

Q43 Fundamentals

What are the pre-requisites to running a Google shopping campaign?

There are a few requirements you'll need to meet to be able to set up a Shopping campaign and create Shopping ads.

Google accounts

You'll need to set up accounts with Google Merchant Center and Google Ads, and link them together.

Policies

Your content for Shopping campaigns and Shopping ads needs to comply with the Shopping ads policies, which are different from the Google Ads policies. You'll need to make sure that your type of business, products, promotions, and website meet the requirements for Shopping ads before you begin advertising.

Product data

You'll need to be able to send us up-to-date product data at least every 30 days. This data needs to meet our standards for data quality. These standards are in place to help provide users with the best shopping experience, and we enforce the standards to help your ads perform better.

The standards for submitting your product data are in the product data specification. You'll use Merchant Center to submit your product data regularly.

Basic product data

The product information you submit using these attributes is our foundation for creating successful ads and free listings for your products. Make sure everything you submit is of the quality you'd show to a customer.

1)id - Your product’s unique identifier

2)title- product's name

3)description- product's description

4)link- product's landing page link

5)image link- The URL of product’s main image

6)availability- in stock, out of stock

7)price- price of product

8)brand- product's brand name

9)gtin- global trade indentification no.(running ads on global level)

Q44 Google Ads

Difference between Maximize clicks and eCPC, when do use them, in what scenarios?

Maximize Clicks is an automated bid strategy that helps you get as many clicks as you can while staying within your budget. The simplest way to bid for clicks is with Maximize Clicks; you simply set a budget, and Google Ads takes care of the rest. For your ad groups, keywords, and placements, you are not required to select specific bid values. The Google Ads system automatically sets your maximum cost-per-click (CPC) bids on your behalf when you use the Maximize Clicks tool, aiming to get you the most clicks within that budget. Campaigns on the Display Network with the marketing objective "Engage with content" or campaigns on apps are not eligible for Maximize Clicks. Adjustments to bids based on day and time use cases are appropriate for product and brand consideration objectives campaigns when we want to increase website traffic, regardless of.

Enhanced cost-per-click (ECPC) helps you get more conversions from manual bidding. In order for ECPC to function, your manual bids for clicks on your website that appear more or less likely to result in a sale or conversion are automatically adjusted. When optimising for conversions, ECPC will attempt to keep your average CPC below the maximum CPC you set (including bid adjustments), in contrast to Target CPA and Target ROAS Smart Bidding, which automatically set bids based on your cost per conversion and return on ad spend targets. In order to keep your cost per conversion the same as it would be with manual bidding, ECPC works to increase conversions for Search, Display, and Hotel campaigns. When used in shopping campaigns, ECPC aids in boosting conversions while attempting to keep spending flat overall. Although not to the full extent of other Smart Bidding strategies, such as Target CPA and Target ROAS, ECPC is a type of Smart Bidding that uses a wide range of auction-time signals, such as browser, location, and time of day, to tailor bids to the particular context of each search. On the Search Network and the Display Network, ECPC is accessible, but not for campaigns involving app instals.

When to use it: When we have a good idea of what the bid might be, but we want the auction to be a little unpredictable so that we don't lose out on a conversion opportunity. It is uitable for sales campaigns during special season or increse in competition days.

Q45 Fundamentals

Suppose we're running some campaigns on Facebook and suddenly they stopped delivering results, what could be the probable reasons behind it?

The following are some frequent causes of Facebook Ads underperformance:

audience is too tiny – Facebook advertisements won't run if there are less than 1,000 active people in your target audience. This could happen for a number of reasons, such as that the targeting parameters you selected don't include enough users, that you're excluding almost all of your audience in an effort to be effective, that the individuals on your customer upload list didn't match as many of your expectations, or that your targeting layers are configured incorrectly.

For those of you wanting to be exceedingly, incredibly focused with your Facebook advertising and reach only a limited number of people, this may therefore be leading to Under delivery of the advertisement.

Another factor can be the limited or disapproved nature of the ads. Similar to audience size restrictions, Facebook has limitations concerning the types of advertisements you are permitted to run on the platform. The amount of text you can fit into an image is limited. Each ad creative's image may only include 20% text; if there is more, impressions may be limited or terminated altogether.

OR

Because Facebook has a responsibility to keep the site engaging and enjoyable for its users, your ad has extremely low or very poor engagement. Accordingly, adverts for ad campaigns aren't shown as frequently as those with high levels of positive engagement when there is low, no, or negative engagement.

Q47 Google Ads

What are the mandatory components of a UTM?

UTM stands for Urchin Traffic Monitor. A UTM code is a simple snippet code that we can add to the end of a URL to track the clicks and performance of campaigns and content.

UTM codes have two components:

1. Tracking variable:

UTM codes have a unique variable that identifies the dimension we are tracking (such as the name of the traffic source). The variable always comes after the "=" sign. The variable after the equals sign may only have letters, numbers, periods, hyphens, and a "+" sign.

2. UTM parameter: The UTM parameter starts with "utm_" and there are five different parameters we can track, i.e., utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, and utm_term.

utm_source:

This parameter allows us to track the source of our traffic. The sources we could track include Bing, Google, Facebook, Instagram, or other individual sources from our marketing channels.

utm_medium:

This parameter tracks what marketing channels our visitors came from. Popular marketing channels include social media, organic search, PPC, email, and affiliates.

utm_campaign:

This tracks which marketing efforts or campaigns attracted our visitors to our site.

utm_content:

The content parameter is usually optional and only used if we have multiple links that go to the same URL. For instance, we may have two CTAs in one email. The content UTM helps us to see the exact link or CTA that was clicked.

utm_term:

The term UTM parameter is used to track keyword terms. This parameter is typically used for paid search ads.

Q48 Google Ads

What are the different versions of app campaigns on Google

When we choose “App promotion” as our goal, we can choose from three campaign subtypes: “App installs,” “App engagement,” and “App pre-registration (Android only).” Each campaign subtype focuses on different actions and bid strategies:

App installs

It run ads that encourage people to install our app.

To help us get the best value from each download, Google Ads also automates targeting and bidding. We can optimize our campaign targeting to focus on finding valuable users based on actions we care about, like in-app conversions.

App engagement

App campaigns for engagement can help us to re-engage customers who've installed our app and encourage them to take specific, in-app actions. Our ads can appear across multiple Google properties, including Google Search, YouTube, Google Play, and within other apps on the Display Network.

App pre-registration (Android only)

It run ads that build excitement and awareness for our apps and games before they are launched on Google Play. After we make our app or game available for pre-registration in our Play Console, we can create an App campaign for the title. People that click on the ad can then pre-register for our app or game from the Play store.

Our ads will be eligible to appear across several Google's properties which includes Google Search, Google Play, YouTube, the Google Display Network, AdMob, Discover on Google Search, Google's search partners, and many more publishers who host app ads.

Q49 Strategy & Planning

Campaign structure for a new brand who is selling "Watches"

I would follow three steps for Facebook: awareness, consideration, and conversion.

I would use an awareness campaign to target watch enthusiasts and brand enthusiasts for companies like Titan, Fastrack, and Casio. I would also use one ad group to target brand website visitors. In order to acquire the maximum results from our money, I will use a video ad creative and optimise my awareness campaign for throughplays. I will also employ the highest volume bid approach. Additionally, the highest volume is the most advised method for awareness advertising.

I'll construct a custom audience of video watchers who watch 50% of my awareness campaign's video ad during the consideration stage. Additionally, I'll retarget website visitors. The advertisement will once more be a video, but this time it will highlight different aspects of our watch. In order to maximise the impact of our budget, I will choose for the highest volume bid method.

Since they are at the bottom of our funnel, I will focus on cart abandoners throughout the conversion stage. I'll specifically target the consideration campaign's video viewers as well. I'll also aim for the 1% of previous buyers who resemble them. The call to action in the advertisement will bring viewers to the product page via a variety of images. In order to maximise the impact of our budget, I will choose for the highest volume bid method.

For Google:-

We'll launch video advertising on YouTube for the awareness stage. People interested in watches and accessories will be our target affinity audience.

In order to reach market audiences who are actively searching to purchase watches, we will run video and image advertising on Youtube and display networks throughout the consideration stage.

In order to increase conversion rates, we will run video and picture advertising on YouTube and other display networks while focusing on a specific audience of people who have already seen our awareness and consideration campaign commercials.

Additionally, we'll run advertisements on the Google Search Network, where we'll split our campaigns into three categories: Brand, Generic, and Competitor. Each group consists of two campaigns: an exact match campaign and a phrase match campaign. Negative keywords will be included whenever necessary to prevent cross-triggering. There will be 10 to 15 appropriate keywords in each ad group. Additionally, each ad group would have a distinct set of ad copies with a range of extensions, increasing the clickability of the search advertising.

Q50 Fundamentals

What's the difference between SEM Vs SMM Vs Programmatic Advertising?

SEM, SMM, and Programmatic ads, all depends on paid ads, but they are a lot different from one another.

SEM stands for Search Engine Marketing and SMM stands for Social Media Marketing.

Search Engine Marketing is the practice of running paid advertisements on search engines to place our website at the top of the SERP and on the side of search engine results pages to gain more visibility and priority than the organic results.

Social Media Marketing is a process in which different social platform are used over internet for promotion of the product or services offered by a company. It is also termed as viral marketing or influencing marketing.

Programmatic advertising is the real-time buying and selling of ad inventory through an automated bidding system. Programmatic advertising enables brands or agencies to purchase ad impressions on publisher sites or apps through a sophisticated ecosystem.

SMM works on social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter etc.

SEM works on search engine Result pages like Google, Bing etc.

Programmatic advertising includes ad slots for display, video and audio ads.
